_about: Fire-safety design factors for crewed systems. 'coverage' codes what the AeroFox evidence base contains for each gravity regime: direct (measured in that regime), partial (related data or literature only), none. 'priority_basis' gives the explicit rule used to order factors; there are no numeric risk scores. Evidence IDs refer to data/findings/findings.json and data/curated/literature_evidence.json.
priority_rules: Tier 1 (decisive): the factor was a primary cause in a fatal or mission-ending NASA fire/oxygen incident in the evidence base, AND the target design condition lies outside the conditions tested in PSI.
Tier 2 (major): the factor was implicated in an incident or controls fire growth in measured data, but the design condition is covered by evidence.
Tier 3 (supporting): the factor changes consequences or recovery; evidence is indirect.

factors.name: Cabin atmosphere (O2 fraction and total pressure)
factors.why: Higher O2 concentration or partial pressure generally raises flammability; materials are historically qualified to 30% O2 at sea-level pressure, while Artemis surface atmospheres target 34% O2 at 56.5 kPa (MOC 37%). Apollo 1's 100% O2 cabin made a wiring fire spread too fast to escape.
questions: Planned total pressure and O2 fraction (and control band)?
Which materials were qualified at that O2 level?
verification: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 at the worst-case O2 of the control band

factors.name: Material flammability and fuel load
factors.why: 1-g upward screening was conservative for thin silicone in Saffire-II at 22% O2 and 20 cm/s, but flame spread in reduced gravity depends on flow and O2; some materials are reported more flammable in lunar gravity than in 1 g.
questions: Which pass NASA-STD-6001 at the design atmosphere?
verification: Material testing at the design atmosphere

factors.name: Ignition sources: electrical systems, batteries, heaters
factors.why: Apollo 1 originated near arcing wiring; Apollo 13 began with heater thermostats not rated for a 65 V supply that damaged Teflon wire insulation inside an O2 tank. The PSI combustion snapshot contains no battery-failure measurements.
verification: Battery thermal-runaway tests at cabin atmosphere
Electrical ignition testing in the design O2

factors.name: Oxygen generation and storage hardware
factors.why: Apollo 13 (O2 tank) and Mir (solid-fuel O2 generator) were oxygen-system failures; the Mir flame blocked an escape route and smoke filled the modules.
questions: Type of O2 source (tanks, generators, electrolysis)
Isolation and location relative to egress paths

factors.name: Ventilation and forced flow
factors.why: In microgravity the forced flow sets the oxygen supply to a flame. Saffire-II sample 2-6 spread 24% faster than 2-5 at 25 vs 20 cm/s (n = 1 each). Ventilation also carries smoke to detectors and between modules.
questions: Can ventilation be shut down per compartment?

factors.name: Smoke and fire detection
factors.why: Smoke from overheated spacecraft materials is sub-micrometre (SAME-R median AMD 0.11-0.36 um by material). Detector alarm performance cannot be inferred from the PSI tables. Optical flame-out is not a reliable end-of-event signal (FLEX-035). Lunar dust can cause nuisance alarms.
verification: Detector testing with representative smoke and dust

factors.name: Suppression and inerting
factors.why: FLEX measured extinction of droplet flames with CO2 and He dilution; helium raised burning rates relative to N2 at equal O2 in FLEX, so inert choice matters. BASS-II lowered O2 by N2 dilution. Cool flames can persist after visible extinction.
verification: Suppression tests on representative fuels at the design atmosphere

factors.name: Crew egress and isolation
factors.why: Apollo 1 led to a quick-opening hatch; on Mir the fire blocked access to an escape vehicle. Escape routes must not pass compartments with O2 sources.

factors.name: Combustion products and post-fire recovery
factors.why: Apollo 1 crew died of asphyxia from CO and toxic gases. Mir's life support needed hours to clear smoke. BASS-II recorded CO rising with O2 consumption.
questions: Atmosphere scrubbing capacity after a fire

factors.name: Partial-gravity fire behaviour
factors.why: Flame spread is non-monotonic in gravity: LUCI measured slower downward spread over SIBAL in simulated lunar gravity than in 1 g, while FM2 cites materials more flammable at lunar gravity. No Mars-gravity data exist in the sources examined.
